title: Physical Geography Terms
description: Common landforms and water features, from deltas and fjords to moraines and atolls. Useful for geography classes and map lovers.
subject: geography

cards.definition: Landform built from sediment deposited where a river slows and spreads out as it enters a sea, lake, or larger river.
Narrow strip of land with water on both sides that connects two larger landmasses.
Long, narrow, deep inlet of the sea between steep cliffs, carved out by a glacier.
Group or chain of islands clustered together.
Piece of land surrounded by water on three sides and attached to a larger landmass.
Narrow natural waterway that connects two larger bodies of water.
Partly enclosed coastal area where fresh water from a river mixes with salt water from the sea.
Stream or river that flows into a larger river.
All the land that drains into a particular river, lake, or other body of water; also called a drainage basin.
Large, relatively flat area of land raised well above the surrounding terrain.
Flat-topped landform with steep sides that is wider than it is tall.
Isolated flat-topped hill with steep sides, smaller than a mesa and usually taller than it is wide.
Looping bend in a river, formed as the current erodes the outer bank and deposits sediment on the inner bank.
U-shaped lake that forms when a river meander is cut off from the main channel.
Flat land beside a river that is built up by sediment deposited during floods.
Fan-shaped deposit of sediment that forms where a stream flows out of steep terrain onto flatter ground.
Ridge or mound of rock and soil debris carried and deposited by a glacier.
Bowl-shaped hollow carved into a mountainside by the head of a glacier.
Ring-shaped coral reef or chain of coral islands that encloses a lagoon.
Shallow body of water separated from the sea by a reef, sandbar, or barrier island.
Long, steep slope or cliff that separates two relatively level areas at different elevations.
Point of high land that juts out into the sea, often with steep cliffs.
